Crypto News Brief: Crypto opens the week deep in Fear despite easing macro pressures — softer oil, lower Treasury yields, a U.S.–Iran de-escalation. Instead, a spreading $89M Coldcard wallet exploit and stalled U.S. legislation are dragging Bitcoin back under $63K. 🚨 Coldcard Wallet Exploit Nears $89 Million A firmware flaw dating to a March 2021 Coldcard build let attackers reconstruct wallet seed phrases and drain roughly 1,367 BTC — close to $89 million — from about 4,585 addresses across three waves, according to Galaxy Research. The bug routed key generation through weak software randomness instead of the device's hardware RNG. A possible fourth sweep surfaced Monday, with some estimates pushing potential losses toward $114 million and rattling confidence in cold storage. Read full story → 📉 Bitcoin Slides Under $63K as Security Fears Trump Macro Relief Bitcoin dipped about 1% to near $62,800 and ether fell toward $1,858 on Monday, even as oil prices eased, Treasury yields slipped, and a U.S.–Iran de-escalation lifted broader risk sentiment. Analysts pinned crypto's weakness on wallet-specific security fears rather than macro forces, with the Fear & Greed Index parked deep in "Fear" territory at 28. More details → 🏛️ CLARITY Act Left Off Senate Agenda, Set to Miss Recess Deadline The Digital Asset Market Clarity Act was absent from Monday's Senate schedule, with no floor vote or cloture motion filed and only a handful of session days left before the early-August recess. Prediction markets have slashed 2026 passage odds to roughly 28%, as unresolved ethics provisions and a crowded calendar push the market-structure bill toward September at the earliest. Read more → 🏦 BitMine Adds ETH as Strategy Sells Bitcoin Again Tom Lee's BitMine bought another 10,399 ETH last week, lifting holdings toward 5.8 million ether — about 4.8% of supply — while repurchasing 4.5 million of its own shares. Meanwhile Strategy trimmed 1,638 BTC (around $105 million) to fund a preferred-stock buyback, underscoring a widening split between bitcoin- and ether-focused corporate treasuries. 76905.subject: Data & Insights: DEX Ratio New Highs; Hood Diversity
76905.body:
The Data and Insights newsletter brings the highlights of the week from The Block’s Data Dashboard

( https://www.theblock.co/data/crypto-markets/spot )

Gm data enjoyers! Before we begin today, if you use a Coldcard for Bitcoin self-custody, we urge you to check on your wallets, as there is an ongoing exploit. Our team recently set up a new newsletter titled " Tokenization Briefing ( https://www.theblock.co/newsletters )." With trillions of dollars of real-world assets migrating onto blockchain rails we are introducing a way for readers to keep up to date with market insights and visual analyses on what matters in the world of Tokenization. Sign up *here* ( https://www.theblock.co/newsletters ).

This week, we’re taking a look at onchain equity trading and CEX volumes. We’ll also look at Pump.fun revenue numbers and last week's earnings from Robinhood and Coinbase. So grab a drink, take a seat, and let's dive in.

1: I'm Something of an Equities Trader Myself

( https://www.theblock.co/data/on-chain-metrics/hyperliquid )

Chart via The Block's Data Dashboard

*Key Insights* provided by The Block Research

* Hyperliquid’s top 10 markets by volume last week have a combined total of ~$32B, but crypto's share has been shrinking. We’ve covered HIP-3’s growing market share before, so we wanted to break it down today.

* BTC and ETH combined for just ~$11B of the total, while the remaining ~$21B came almost entirely from tokenized equities and indices deployed through HIP-3.
* SK Hynix (SKHX) alone did roughly $5.6B, more than ETH, with Micron (MU), SanDisk (SNDK), and the DRAM index rounding out a memory-and-semiconductor-heavy list alongside the Nasdaq 100 (XYZ100) and S&P 500 (SP500) trackers.

* Notably, there have been days where SKHX's daily volume has individually cleared bitcoin's, a threshold that would have been unthinkable for a tokenized stock a year ago. This speaks to how quickly HIP-3 volume has scaled to $4B in open interest.
* Nearly all of that equity volume runs through TradeXYZ, the HIP-3 deployer behind the "xyz:" tickers. They already account for the vast majority of HIP-3 open interest and volume.

* Every HIP-3 market inherits HyperCore's shared orderbook and the HLP vault's market-making depth from day one rather than bootstrapping its own, reinforcing the competitive liquidity moat that Hyperliquid has built.

See the Interactive Chart ( https://www.theblock.co/data/on-chain-metrics/hyperliquid )

2: The new CEX?

( https://www.theblock.co/data/decentralized-finance/dex-non-custodial/dex-to-cex-spot-trade-volume )

Chart via The Block's Data Dashboard

*Key Insights* provided by The Block Research

* The DEX to CEX ratio has closed the month at a new all-time high of 24% and up from 17% just a year ago. The chart tracks spot exchange volume, separate from futures and derivatives, which measures trades on DEXs like Uniswap and Aerodrome.

* A large factor in this rise has been a softening o
